gen-dafont-groovy-gf-golos-text: Groovy's c nearly shuts itself, leaving just a thin slit. Golos Text, a plain sans, fills the line with tall lowercase and an s that opens wide, so paragraphs of it move along without any fuss.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-hedvig-letters-sans: Funky, loose and a bit cheeky, Groovy spaces its lowercase out with a grin. Hedvig Letters Sans, a plain sans, lets its c gape wide and keeps small letters nearly capital height, so the two settle into a good rhythm.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-heebo: Groovy draws its arms and legs at constant width, with almost no stroke contrast. Heebo is a sans-serif with a tall middle band and curves that stop short of closing, so a modest bump in its size would help it hold its own beneath that heading.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-hind-guntur: Groovy's c pinches almost shut, which gives it a tight, playful look. Hind Guntur is a plain sans with wide gaps at its curve ends and stamped-metal tall lowercase, and that openness gives the heading room to be loud.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-hind-madurai: Friendly and funky, Groovy loosens its lowercase and nearly seals each c, which gives the heading plenty of personality. Blow Hind Madurai up large and it would crowd the sans-serif look.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-hind-mysuru: Hind Mysuru is a plain sans whose lowercase presses up near ascender height and whose a keeps its mouth ajar. Groovy's near-closed c is the foil.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-hind-siliguri: Hind Siliguri hums along in a flat gray texture, its rounds split like a cracked bangle. Giving it a touch more size than the heading's neighbors would help it stand up to Groovy's loose, funky lowercase.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-hind-vadodara: Groovy's narrow slit, where the c almost closes, gives it a cheeky wink. Hind Vadodara, a plain sans, answers with spacious terminal gaps and tall-bowled e and a, making openness the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-huninn: Groovy nearly seals its c, leaving only a slit, and spaces its lowercase loosely. Huninn, a sans, keeps its s terminals clear of the body and lifts its lowercase close to cap height, so a long read feels sturdy.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-karla: Karla reads stocky and a little blunt, with a gaping c and a middle band so tall it fills the line. Karla, a plain sans, would carry a long passage with a friendly, modern ease beside Groovy's funky heading.
